      <p>I develop interpretable statistical models for prediction, ranking and comparison under uncertainty.   <article class="expertise-area" id="optimisation">
    <div class="expertise-area-heading"><span>02</span><h2>Optimisation & decision science</h2></div>
    <div class="expertise-area-copy">
      <p>I formulate problems in terms of objectives, constraints and trade-offs, then develop methods for finding useful solutions. My research covers convex optimisation, conditional-gradient methods, optimal transport and variational models; the transferable skill is choosing and validating an approach that respects the structure of the real problem.</p>
      <ul class="expertise-skill-list"><li>Convex and constrained optimisation</li><li>Conditional-gradient and sparse methods</li><li>Optimal transport and variational modelling</li><li>Scenario analysis and decision support</li></ul>
      <p class="expertise-evidence"><a href="projects.html">Optimisation projects →</a><a href="publications.html#2024-Bre-Car-Fan-Wal">Representative publication →</a></p>
    </div>
  </article>

  <article class="expertise-area" id="scientific-computing">
    <div class="expertise-area-heading"><span>03</span><h2>Scientific computing & reproducible workflows</h2></div>
    <div class="expertise-area-copy">
      <p>I translate mathematical and statistical ideas into computational experiments using Python, R and MATLAB. This includes numerical algorithms, simulation, data analysis, visualisation and structured publishing workflows. I value implementations that make assumptions visible and allow results to be reproduced and scrutinised.</p>
      <ul class="expertise-skill-list"><li>Python, R and MATLAB</li><li>Numerical simulation and algorithm implementation</li><li>Reproducible analysis and structured data</li><li>Quarto, LaTeX, Markdown, Git and web publishing</li></ul>

  <article class="expertise-area" id="inverse-problems">
    <div class="expertise-area-heading"><span>04</span><h2>Inverse problems, imaging & complex systems</h2></div>
    <div class="expertise-area-copy">
      <p>Inverse problems ask how to recover an unknown quantity from incomplete, indirect or noisy observations. My work combines physical structure, regularisation and optimisation to make that recovery stable, with particular experience in dynamic imaging and MRI. The same reasoning is relevant whenever the quantity of interest cannot be observed directly.</p>
      <ul class="expertise-skill-list"><li>Ill-posed problems and regularisation</li><li>Dynamic data and motion-aware models</li><li>Noise, undersampling and uncertainty</li><li>Mathematical imaging and signal reconstruction</li></ul>
      <p class="expertise-evidence"><a href="research.html#inverse-problems-research">Research theme →</a><a href="https://github.com/sfanzon/DGCG_algorithm">DGCG implementation →</a></p>
    </div>
  </article>
